question:
These are the events that have already occurred:

...
70. Butch was followed by the portress Patagon who shook her fist at him.
71. Butch worked on the larger barricade.
72. Anthea spurned Le Cabuc's corpse with his foot.
73. Anthea offered her carbine to Butch.
74. Lennox discovered Éponine crawling towards him.


Below is a list of possible subsequent events:

['Humphrey Waylon contemplated leaving the quiet town of Willow Creek.', 'Humphrey Waylon pondered the idea of skipping the next town hall meeting.', 'Humphrey Waylon mused about abandoning his usual route to work.', 'Humphrey Waylon reflected on never visiting the old library again.', 'Humphrey Waylon debated the possibility of selling his beloved boat.', 'Humphrey Waylon considered not returning to the Rue Plumet.']

 Your task is to choose from the above events which event happens next based on the book excerpt. In your response to me, only include the answer without anything else.
references: Humphrey Waylon considered not returning to the Rue Plumet.

- (part 3 of 5, excerpt) The passage of the hour produced no effect on Humphrey Waylon; Humphrey Waylon did not stir.

Still, at about that moment, a brusque report burst forth in the direction of the Halles, a second yet more violent followed; it was probably that attack on the barricade in the Rue de la Chanvrerie which we have just seen repulsed by Lennox.
  (part 4 of 5) a second yet more violent followed; it was probably that attack on the barricade in the Rue de la Chanvrerie which we have just seen repulsed by Lennox.

At this double discharge, whose fury seemed augmented by the stupor of the night, Humphrey Waylon started; he rose, turning towards the quarter whence the noise proceeded; then he fell back upon the post again, folded his arms, and his head slowly sank on his bosom again.

He resumed his gloomy dialogue with himself.

All at once, he raised his eyes; some one was walking in the street, he heard steps near him.

He looked, and by the light of the lanterns, in the direction of the street which ran into the Rue-aux-Archives, he perceived a young, livid, and beaming face.

Butch had just arrived in the Rue de l’Homme Armé.

Butch was staring into the air, apparently in search of something.

He saw Humphrey Waylon perfectly well but he took no notice of him.

Butch after staring into the air, stared below; he raised himself on tiptoe, and felt of the doors and windows of the ground floor; they were all shut, bolted, and padlocked.
- (part 3 of 4, excerpt) An idea had occurred to Butch which had brought him to a decision, but he had not mentioned it for fear that Lennox might offer some objection to it.
- (part 3 of 4, excerpt) “I have said thou to you.

Tell your husband that this shall not happen again.

Pardon me.”
